headline: Bitcoin is stuck near $64,000-65,000 as US tech stocks fall more than 2% and the dollar climbs, Fed Chair Warsh gave no hint on rates, and two DeFi platforms were hit by exploits.

market.asOf: Read at about 19:56-19:58 UTC Mon 16 Nov (about 02:56 Tue Bangkok) from the CoinGecko and CoinMarketCap homepages; CoinGecko prices shown. CoinGecko had BTC at $64,741 and CoinMarketCap at $64,929. The 24-hour change is left out because the pages read did not show whether it was up or down, and the two sites gave different sizes. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.

stories.title: Bitcoin stuck near $64,000-65,000 as tech stocks slide and the dollar hits a 19-month high
stories.summary: Bitcoin bounced to about $65,500 after the US stock market opened on Monday but could not hold $65,000. Tech stocks fell more than 2% and the US dollar rose to its strongest since April 2025, a mix that tends to weigh on crypto. Shares of crypto companies fell harder than bitcoin itself.
points: Bitcoin rose to about $65,500 after the US open, per CoinDesk's live coverage, then fell back to $64,010 on Bitstamp, per Cointelegraph.
At 1:34pm ET the Nasdaq was down 2.5% and Nvidia down 4.8%, and at 2:36pm ET the dollar index was at its highest since April 2025, per CoinDesk's live coverage.
Coinbase shares were at $119.64 (down 6.27%) and Strategy (MSTR) at $103.33 (down 7.43%) at about 15:09 UTC, per CryptoTicker.
Bitcoin is down 17% in November and has had six weekly losses in a row, per CoinDesk's live coverage.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $185.5M on Friday 13 November, their seventh straight day of outflows, and about $2.35B so far in November, per CoinCentral.

stories.title: Fed Chair Warsh talks about AI, not interest rates; focus moves to Wednesday's Fed minutes
stories.summary: In his noon ET speech in San Francisco, Fed Chair Warsh talked about how artificial intelligence could change the economy and gave no signal on interest rates. That removes one event from the week but changes nothing for traders who already expect a December rate rise. Higher rates tend to pull money away from risky assets like crypto.
points: Warsh said Fed staff are modelling three 'illustrative scenarios, not forecasts', including one where super intelligence ('SI') could disappoint and 'equity valuations could fall, leading to an economic slowdown', per his speech on the Federal Reserve's website.
The AP reported that Warsh 'steers clear' of AI's inflation risk.
Before the speech, a 0.25-point December rate rise was fully priced in by futures traders, with about 13% odds of 0.5 points, per Pomegra. That is a market bet, not a Fed decision.
The US 10-year Treasury yield was 5.116% on Monday morning, versus 4.83% a week earlier, per CoinDesk's live coverage.
Minutes of the Fed's October meeting come out Wednesday at 2pm ET, per CoinDesk.

sources.label: AP via WDBO: Warsh on AI

stories.title: Lighter pauses withdrawals after an exploit; a Gnosis Safe wallet is drained of $6.45M
stories.summary: Lighter, a decentralized exchange for futures trading, paused all withdrawals on Monday after an attacker used a leaked access key to drain one trader's account. Lighter says its smart contracts were not affected. Separately, a Gnosis Safe shared wallet lost about $6.45M. They follow October's Binance hack and are a reminder that funds on DeFi platforms can be frozen or lost.
points: Lighter blamed a leaked API key for one trader's account and said 'The protocol and smart contracts were unaffected', per CoinDesk.
Estimates of Lighter's loss differ: $10.4M traced by Bitquery, per CoinDesk; other researchers cited by CoinDesk put it at $15.5M across two accounts. Lighter has not confirmed a figure.
Lighter's LIT token fell more than 10% to under $2.48, then recovered to $2.62, per CoinDesk.
A Gnosis Safe multisig wallet lost about $6.45M, including about $4.30M of USDC, through a compromised or misconfigured module, per CoinGape.

briefs.title: Strategy buys only 485 bitcoin
briefs.summary: Strategy bought 485 BTC for $33.4M at an average $68,887, taking it to 850,849 BTC at an average cost of $75,452, per Investing.com.

briefs.title: Arbitrum vote on frozen Binance-hack funds
briefs.summary: An Arbitrum DAO vote on returning 8,425.997 ETH and about 74.56M ARB to Binance, subject to legal indemnification, was due to end 16 November, per CoinDesk. No result had been reported when this was written.

briefs.title: Bitmine keeps adding ether
briefs.summary: Bitmine bought 7,653 ETH (about $15M), taking its holdings to about 6.07M ETH, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Harvard holds bitcoin ETF shares
briefs.summary: A filing shows Harvard's endowment held 3.045M shares of BlackRock's IBIT, worth $144M, at 30 September, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Solana ETFs see six weeks of outflows
briefs.summary: SOL hit a weekend low of $67.41 and US Solana ETFs have had six straight weekly outflows totalling $197.4M, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Russia opens crypto to ordinary investors
briefs.summary: From 17 November non-qualified retail investors in Russia can buy BTC, ETH and USDT up to annual limits, and exchanges may begin organised trading from 22 November if their rules are approved, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: US crypto market bill faces a reset
briefs.summary: The CLARITY Act's Senate vote failed 49-50 in September, and the Senate Banking Committee holds a hearing on SEC nominees Levine and Johnson on 19 November, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: US moves to seize $1.2B tied to the Binance hack
briefs.summary: The Justice Department is targeting $1.2B in stolen crypto linked to North Korea's Binance hack, per CoinDesk (12 November).
